title: Allocator drift causing token emission sag after dedicated runtime rollout
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Customer escalation: multiple enterprise customers (Dedicated + Private) observed sudden increases in first-token time (TTFT) and sustained token/sec degradation after we rolled out allocator changes in runtime-2.4.1. The regression appears under mixed-quant and long-context workloads and is amplified during variant probing and canary fanout. Hosted customers saw degraded p95 but less severe than Dedicated due to different allocator config. Initial hypothesis: allocator heuristics now bias towards microbatching small requests which increases KV cache churn and causes prefetch thrashing on longer contexts, producing token emission sag and jitter.
steps_taken: 03-14 03:20 UTC: Oncall triaged — confirmed TTFT spike correlates with runtime-2.4.1 rollout window and specific allocator commit (git sha: a1b2c3d)
03-14 04:00 UTC: Pulled live profiler traces from affected Dedicated clusters — observed increased mutex contention inside Allocator::reserve and elevated KV cache miss ratio for contexts > 4k tokens
03-14 05:15 UTC: Deployed additional telemetry flags to record microbatch sizes and per-request warmup counts (temporary sampling at 10%)
03-14 08:40 UTC: Reproduced locally with a long-context, mixed-quant model (LlamaX-30B-int8) using our canary harness — reproduced token/sec drop and observed repeated small microbatch allocations

03-14 10:00 UTC: Scoped mitigation — reverted allocator heuristic change for Dedicated clusters behind the canary gate and applied emergency configuration that forces minimum microbatch size of 8 for long-context variants
03-14 13:30 UTC: Notified affected customers and provided temporary mitigation steps (route traffic to older variant or pin to prior runtime), opened customer-facing incident notes
decisions: Roll-forward patch: implement allocator backpressure heuristic that biases away from microbatching for contexts > 2k tokens (chosen to avoid full rollback and provide targeted fix)
Keep canary off for next 24h for Dedicated and Private until patch validated; Hosted to remain under monitoring with aggressive telemetry sampling
Add integration test covering mixed-quant + long-context microbatch allocation to prevent regression
next_steps: 03-15: Ship runtime patch (PR: #5821) to allocator module with unit + integration tests; target deploy to staging by 03-15 10:00 UTC
03-15: Run 6-hour soak on staging and run customer workload replay (contains failing trace) to validate TTFT/tokens/sec recovery
03-16: Gradual rollout to Dedicated canaries with gating on TTFT p95 and tokens/sec thresholds
Post-mortem and release notes due in Cycle 2026-W12; track long-term metric changes and add kernel-level guardrails
